I am reconsidering the Water Works trade. A utility monopoly would not generate enough income to justify spending $200 to $250 before landing on key properties. I also checked whether trading with p1 could help me, but his holdings do not complete any of my color sets.

I am now considering buying St. Charles Place from p2 and States Avenue from p4 to complete a pink monopoly. This would require paying both players, but it would give me a strong set with solid rent. I noted that p2 previously rejected a $250 offer for St. Charles.

I realized that buying Boardwalk for $550 would leave me cash-poor and unable to block Tennessee Avenue. p2 recently purchased Boardwalk and explicitly stated he will not sell it for cash; he only wants serious monopoly-for-monopoly deals. A cash offer would waste a negotiation and reveal desperation, possibly prompting him to demand Park Place in return.

I will end the turn. I will not propose any trades, since repeated offers they already rejected would look desperate and undermine my prior strategy. I will keep my cash and remain consistent.

I am now weighing which unowned properties to bid on. Tennessee Avenue is the most urgent, since p1 needs it to complete his orange set. I am reconsidering a Water Works trade. p4 has only $110 cash and no room to build more brown houses, so he may be willing to sell for $200. I would gain a utility monopoly, but he would receive cash that could help him survive or bid higher in future auctions.

I calculated the expected value of a utility monopoly. The average rent is roughly $15 to $25 per opponent turn, so breaking even would take about three to four full rounds. That is reasonable but not urgent.
